nodes.label: Window/Policy decode contract (window={arrayBuffer,baseOffset,syntax,littleEndian,implicit,decoder}, policy={forceStoreRaw,noCopy,ignoreErrors})
nodes.rationale: Replaces the lazy core's mutable ctx object with two explicit read-only inputs. There is deliberately no isMeta parameter anywhere in decodeCore: callers construct a meta window (original buffer, explicit-LE, no decoder) or a body window (post-inflate buffer, negotiated syntax/endianness, active decoder), so meta/body resolution happens once at the caller instead of via ternaries scattered through the decode path.

nodes.label: decodeCore — shared element-decode core (src/core/decodeCore.js)
nodes.rationale: The 'one read core' (refactor item R3): element-decode primitives (resolveVrInstance, shapeReadValues, decodeElementValues, decodeWithEagerReadTag, classifyElement, resolveCharacterSet, seedReadContext, buildElementStream) were closures trapped inside LazyDicomReader; extracting them lets readFileLazy, fromPart10, and fromPart10Stream share one core with byte-identical behavior. Circular-import discipline: DicomMessage.lookupTag/_readTag/_normalizeSyntax accessed only inside function bodies, never at module evaluation time.

nodes.label: seedReadContext(byteArray, options) — parse + meta/body window construction (deflate-aware via pako inflater)
nodes.rationale: Centralizes parseDicom invocation, syntax normalization, and window construction; for deflated transfer syntax (1.2.840.10008.1.2.1.99) metaWindow indexes the ORIGINAL buffer while bodyWindow indexes the post-inflate buffer, which is what later let fromPart10 handle deflate natively (J4b) and the K3 tail-fallback re-seed a full parse. Meta-group validation and eager-fallback policy deliberately stay in readFileLazy — they are lazy-reader policy, not core.
nodes.norm_label: seedreadcontext(bytearray, options) — parse + meta/body window construction (deflate-aware via pako inflater)

nodes.rationale: The contract was entirely implicit before K0 (zero call sites in src/); it was defined through TDD. Three bugs were fixed in one expression: live mutable buffers array passed instead of chunkIndex; hardcoded 0 instead of logicalOffset; an always-negative Math.min expression instead of byteLength. nodes.label: fromPart10Stream — chunked, bounded-memory bytes→events DICOM streaming source
nodes.rationale: Slice K's deliverable: an async source that accepts AsyncIterable, WHATWG ReadableStream, or single-buffer input, feeds a ReadBufferStream concurrently with parsing (feed unawaited), and emits the same event vocabulary as buffered fromPart10 with bounded memory via ensureAvailable/consume. Built via staged placeholders: K1 API skeleton, K2 incremental FMI, K3 defined-length body, K4 undefined-length + release, K5 streaming deflate.

nodes.label: Decision D-E — streaming source forces noCopy off
nodes.rationale: fromPart10Stream does not accept a noCopy option: zero-copy views would alias chunk memory that consume() releases, so every emitted/retained buffer (FMI values, leaf values, fragments, undefined-leaf windows) must be a fresh slice() copy. Documented in the fromPart10Stream JSDoc and re-verified in K4 when chunk release went live.
nodes.norm_label: decision d-e — streaming source forces nocopy off

nodes.label: Three-way input normalization (ArrayBuffer/Uint8Array, AsyncIterable, WHATWG ReadableStream)
nodes.rationale: Buffer inputs stay re-runnable through the DicomEventStream factory; iterable/ReadableStream inputs are single-use and a second .process() returns a rejected Promise (not a synchronous throw, preserving the await-process contract). ReadableStream detection is global-typeof based so it degrades gracefully to the AsyncIterable branch in sandboxed environments; a dependency-free getReader() loop is the fallback adapter.
nodes.norm_label: three-way input normalization (arraybuffer/uint8array, asynciterable, whatwg readablestream)

nodes.label: Incremental preamble + File Meta Information parsing with buffered startDataSet replay
nodes.rationale: FMI is always explicit-LE and never deflated (PS3.5 §7.1), so it can be header-decoded incrementally from the chunk stream. FMI element events must be buffered until (0002,0010) is decoded because startDataSet must carry the correct transferSyntaxUID — there is no listener contract for correcting it later. Values are copied into fresh ArrayBuffers (FMI is <1KB) to respect D-E aliasing rules. Header framing uses ValueRepresentation.isLength32() for parity by construction rather than a hardcoded extended-VR set.
nodes.norm_label: incremental preamble + file meta information parsing with buffered startdataset replay

nodes.label: K3 staged fallback ladder (deflate buffered / undefined-length tail-fallback / native defined-length)
nodes.rationale: Binding design decision to keep each stage small: deflate keeps the K2 buffered body; an undefined-length element mid-body triggers a tail-fallback (await completeness, seedReadContext, walkBodyTail from the element's start offset) because no events for that element were emitted yet; everything else streams natively. consume() call sites were wired but gated dormant (releaseEnabled=false) so K4 could flip one switch. Top-level SQs buffered their subtree events for fallback atomicity — discard-and-restart on TailFallbackSignal.
nodes.norm_label: k3 staged fallback ladder (deflate buffered / undefined-length tail-fallback / native defined-length)

nodes.label: Implicit-SQ promotion bug in buffered fromPart10 (UN→SQ via data-peek / el.items)
nodes.rationale: Fix-round testing exposed a real divergence: for dictionary-unknown implicit elements whose value starts with an item tag, the parser's internal isSequence peek populates el.items, but resolveVrInstance (dictionary-only) returned UN — so buffered fromPart10 emitted UN where the standard intends SQ. Both fromPart10 (using el.items) and fromPart10Stream (repeating the raw byte peek per readDicomElementImplicit) received the same promotion so the two paths agree. A related pre-existing gap remains ledgered: readFileLazy/decodeCore.resolveVrInstance lacks the data-peek for DEFINED-length unknown implicit elements.
nodes.norm_label: implicit-sq promotion bug in buffered frompart10 (un→sq via data-peek / el.items)

nodes.label: Per-subtree EventBuffer for undefined-length SQ length backfill
nodes.rationale: The brief preferred deleting event buffering entirely, but buffered fromPart10 emits startSequence/startItem with the parser's COMPUTED content span (not on-wire 0xFFFFFFFF), which is unknown until the closing delimiter — and startSequence must precede its items. So defined-length SQ/items emit directly while undefined-length SQ/items buffer subtree events (lambdas with decoded values baked in) just long enough to backfill the span, then flush. Bounded by metadata-sized subtrees (~1.9KB corpus max); pixel data is encapsulated, never SQ, so it streams unbuffered. The K3 tail-fallback EventBuffer role (atomicity) was deleted along with TailFallbackSignal/triggerTailFallback/walkBodyTail.
nodes.norm_label: per-subtree eventbuffer for undefined-length sq length backfill

nodes.label: Chunk release live — clearBuffers:true + consume() at top-level element boundaries
nodes.rationale: After every completed top-level element the stream calls consume(stream.offset), releasing fully-passed chunks (verified by a getBufferMemoryInfo smoke test: final retained totalSize < fileLen/2). Deflate and raw-dataset fallbacks never consume (they need full bytes until K5). Safe under D-E because every retained buffer is a fresh slice() copy. Granularity limit acknowledged: a single huge pixel-data element retains its bytes until it completes; the formal bounded-memory gate is K6.
nodes.norm_label: chunk release live — clearbuffers:true + consume() at top-level element boundaries

nodes.label: Accepted stream-vs-buffered divergences (encapsulated startElement 0xFFFFFFFF; undefined-length text VRs throw loudly)
nodes.rationale: Two documented, test-pinned divergences: (1) emitEncapsulated emits startElement length as on-wire 0xFFFFFFFF instead of buffered's computed span — forced by fragment streaming, since the span is unknown until the closing delimiter and emitting startElement first is what lets fragments arrive before input completes; (2) undefined-length text VRs (UT/UC/UR, non-conformant per PS3.5) — buffered silently swallows the delimiter and trailing elements into a garbage string, the stream throws loudly (stream is BETTER). Both are gate-visible only through dedicated raw-event assertions.
nodes.norm_label: accepted stream-vs-buffered divergences (encapsulated startelement 0xffffffff; undefined-length text vrs throw loudly)

nodes.label: Root bug: pako default chunkSize 65536 deadlocks streaming inflate

nodes.label: Packed Dictionary System
nodes.rationale: Naive object-literal dictionaries cost megabytes of parse/alloc at startup for every importer. Replacing literals with base64-encoded typed-array tables decoded once on first use dropped import cost from 181ms to 19ms (9.5x), keeping hot-path lookups at binary-search-plus-memo cost while keeping startup nearly free.

nodes.rationale: In 0.x the ~5000-entry nameMap was built at import time; 1.0 makes it a memoizing static getter built on first access so import time no longer pays for it. All existing access patterns go through the getter unchanged.

nodes.label: generate/ Dictionary Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Packed modules are build artifacts with documented provenance: generate-dictionary.js downloads PS3.6/PS3.7 docbook XML from dicom.nema.org, pack_dicom.mjs flattens into sorted parallel arrays with dedup'd VR/VM code tables, bench-dictionary-load.mjs is the source of the 181ms-to-19ms measurement.

nodes.label: Event-Stream Contract
nodes.rationale: A hybrid contract: synchronous push core (allocation-free hot path) with an async-iterator adapter for for-await ergonomics. Separates sources, stream, listeners, and retained representation so readers, writers, naturalizers, validators, and anonymizers compose on one contract. Invariants: loss preservation, well-formed nesting, transport-only binary, out-of-band diagnostics, optional sourceSpan.

nodes.label: decodeCore (shared decode module, src/core/decodeCore.js)
nodes.rationale: Stateless module with a two-input contract (window: fully-resolved byte region; policy: decode options) shared by fromPart10 and readFileLazy so both readers use identical value decoding; fromPart10 no longer whole-file delegates to the lazy reader.

nodes.label: Streaming Source Gate Suite (streamEquivalence.test.js)
nodes.rationale: Holds fromPart10Stream to the same contract as fromPart10: corpus x chunking equivalence (1/37/1024/whole-file chunks), raw-event parity, synthesized EBE SQ byte-order check, bounded-memory gates for encapsulated and deflate, backpressure proof, and seven loud-not-silent truncation phases.

nodes.label: Source-Agnostic Equivalence
nodes.rationale: Because all sources emit the same contract, the naturalized object is identical across origins; verified across the whole fixture corpus by naturalizing from raw bytes, parsed dict, and DICOMweb JSON and requiring the three results to match.

nodes.label: dcmjs Layered Architecture (layers 0-2 + adapters)
nodes.rationale: Each layer only knows the layers below: layer 0 the dependency-free offset tokenizer, layer 1 the data model (lazy core, VR classes, writer, dictionary), layer 2 features (anonymizer, SR, derivations), adapters outside the stack consuming the public API. Arrows only point downward; the parser never imports dcmjs, the dictionary, or character sets by design.

nodes.label: The Derivability Argument (offsets over eager values)
nodes.rationale: Offsets can always produce values (decode lazily, with any charset, or never) but eager values can never recover offsets — once decoded, the exact header framing, padding, and delimiters are gone. Recording offsets is therefore the more fundamental representation, enabling both lazy reads and byte-faithful writes; startOffset/endOffset were added because dataOffset alone is ambiguous (header size depends on VR; corrected lengths exclude delimiters).
nodes.norm_label: the derivability argument (offsets over eager values)

nodes.label: fromPart10Stream (chunked streaming source, slice K)
nodes.rationale: Decision D-C: a self-contained ported body loop (await-at-boundaries) rather than adapting the tokenizer, which assumes one contiguous buffer. Decision D-E: noCopy intentionally rejected because zero-copy views alias chunk memory that consume() releases mid-parse. Bounded memory (~336 KB peak for encapsulated) via clearBuffers + per-element/per-fragment consume(); promise-driven backpressure via setDrain/awaitDrain.

nodes.label: AsyncDicomReader (legacy chunk-feed reader)
nodes.rationale: Still runs its own header/element loop with the 4-verb DicomMetadataListener vocabulary and delegates the meta group to the eager DicomMessage._read — the main reason the eager read loop survives in the 1.0 beta. Kept self-contained deliberately; still the right tool for per-frame pixel-data delivery.

nodes.label: SplitDataView (chunk-spanning DataView facade)
nodes.rationale: 1.0 scoped fix: findStart caches the last chunk hit (and checks its successor) before falling back to linear scan, making sequential streaming reads O(1) per primitive instead of O(chunks).

nodes.label: DELTA-A (encapsulated startElement.length divergence)
nodes.rationale: fromPart10Stream carries the on-wire 0xFFFFFFFF for encapsulated pixel data while the buffered path carries a computed span; normalized by name in the gate suite and pinned in code.

nodes.label: DELTA-B (undefined-length text VR loud failure)
nodes.rationale: Deliberate divergence for non-conformant undefined-length UT/UC/UR: the stream fails noisily (truncation throw) where the buffered path silently consumes trailing bytes into a garbage string and loses elements. Loud failure over silent mishandling; pinned by K4 Test 22b.

nodes.label: K7 AsyncDicomReader Re-platform Assessment
nodes.rationale: Deferred to 1.x because two breakage points prevent a thin adapter: uncompressed pixel-data frame splitting (fromPart10Stream delivers one flat binary sub-stream; AsyncDicomReader splits per-frame from tracked geometry) and compressed frame assembly from Basic Offset Table offsets. Options: per-frame events, a frame-assembly adapter, or a comprehensive shim.

nodes.label: Gate Philosophy (bench:parser, bundle gate, dual-core equivalence)
nodes.rationale: Two mechanically enforced rules: never regress the tokenizer (bench:parser geomean <=1.10 vs published dicom-parser@1.8.21, currently ~0.85; gate:parser-bundle proves the parser stays a dependency-free island under 120 kB with no side effects) and both cores stay equivalent until the eager core is deleted (full 635-test suite green on lazy AND DCMJS_CORE=eager).

nodes.label: ISO_IR 192 Normalize-on-Read
nodes.rationale: dcmjs deliberately rewrites SpecificCharacterSet to ["ISO_IR 192"] on read (keeping the original in _rawValue) and encodes strings as UTF-8 on write, so application code only ever sees JavaScript strings and the output file is self-consistent. Whether to keep this quirk versus surfacing the original charset is an open 1.0 API decision.

nodes.label: charsetPassthroughSafe Gate
nodes.rationale: Passthrough is only safe when the writer's UTF-8 normalization is byte-stable against the source: absent/empty/ASCII/UTF-8 top-level charsets only. Deliberately conservative — ISO_IR 100 (Latin-1) sources always re-encode today; a per-element ASCII fast path to widen the gate is planned 1.x work.

nodes.label: Deflated Explicit VR LE Transfer Syntax (1.2.840.10008.1.2.1.99)
nodes.rationale: 0.x silently wrote uncompressed bodies under the deflated TSUID — non-conformant files. 1.0 fixes it: declared syntax and bytes agree; conversion to/from deflated is just a meta edit since the body encoding is ELE on both sides, only the stream-level wrapper changes. Inflation is eager because deflate is a stream-level wrapper — no per-element inflate is possible.
nodes.norm_label: deflated explicit vr le transfer syntax (1.2.840.10008.1.2.1.99)

nodes.label: DicomEventStream (re-runnable source wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Wraps a re-runnable source so one stream can drive several sinks (toNaturalized, toDicomWebJson, toPart10, toDataSet, process, asyncIterable). Byte-identical Part 10 round-tripping is an explicit non-goal of this pipeline — that is served by lazy read + passthrough writer; the event pipeline produces semantically faithful output.

nodes.label: Naturalized Model (VM-driven cardinality)
nodes.rationale: The shape of each value follows the attribute's declared VM, not how many values happen to be present — the contract that replaces defensive Array.isArray guards. Keyword keys, PN component objects that stringify to raw PN, single-item sequences readable straight through, creator-grouped private tags, precision-preserving over-precision strings, and a configurable cardinality-violation policy.

nodes.label: @dcmjs/fhir (FHIR sink)
nodes.rationale: Strict-out contract: standard FHIR only (no ids, meta.tags, or endpoint references — deployment decisions the consumer decorates), R4/R4B only (anything else throws rather than emitting unverified shapes), and identity-less input returns null rather than a hollow resource. Follows the IHE Radiology (MADO) mapping.

nodes.label: Instance-Driven Single-Value Collapse
nodes.rationale: The 0.x rule carried into 1.0-beta unchanged: a one-element Value array collapses to a scalar, so the same attribute can be a scalar in one file and an array in another — the single most common dcmjs 0.x complaint, and the subject of the open VM-driven-shapes 1.0 decision.

nodes.label: naturalizedRules Catalog (dcmjs/schema, normative)
nodes.rationale: One machine-readable source of truth for the naturalized representation; the rule catalog is normative and the TypeScript and JSON-Schema documents are generated from it so they cannot drift. dictionaryHash ties the artifact to the exact dictionary edition. CI enforces freshness/determinism, type correctness, and code agreement against NaturalizedListener output over the full fixture corpus.

nodes.label: TypeScript Projection (types/dcmjs-schema.d.ts, NaturalizedDataset)
nodes.rationale: Types the naturalized data shape only, not the dcmjs API — which is why it ships as the dcmjs/schema subpath rather than a top-level types field. 64-bit integers type as number|string so precision is never silently lost.

nodes.label: JSON-Schema Projection (naturalized.schema.json)
nodes.rationale: A projection for ecosystem tooling (Ajv etc.); streaming element-by-element validation consumes the catalog directly because JSON Schema cannot express DICOM VM patterns like 3-3n or original-encoding length caps. x-dicom-vr/vm/tag annotations carry what JSON Schema cannot.

nodes.label: Assignment-Based Editing Rules
nodes.rationale: Assignments (entry.Value=, entry._rawValue=, upsertTag) are tracked at any depth and dirty the enclosing SQ chain; in-place mutation of a materialized value is undetectable and silently discarded by the passthrough writer. Structural sequence edits (item count, key adds/deletes) ARE detected at write time; leaf in-place mutation and identical-key-set item swaps remain undetectable.

nodes.label: writeOptions (allowInvalidVRLength, fragmentMultiframe)
nodes.rationale: allowInvalidVRLength gates write-time validation on the re-encode path only — byte-faithful passthrough legitimately preserves invalid stored lengths, so a no-edit rewrite of a file with an over-long value succeeds even with the default false. fragmentMultiframe:false asks for bytes the source does not contain, so it disables passthrough for the whole dict.

nodes.label: dcmjs (library introduction, the 1.0 story)
nodes.rationale: 1.0 merges two long-lived projects into one engine: the dicom-parser tokenizer became dcmjs's read core, reading is lazy by default, the writer is byte-faithful, and everything lives in one pnpm monorepo. Grew out of the OHIF and QIICR communities; ~15,000 weekly npm downloads on the 0.x line as of early 2025.

nodes.label: dcmjs Before and After 1.0 (side-by-side)
nodes.rationale: The code you write barely changes — the engine underneath changed completely. 0.x paid for everything twice (decode all on read, re-encode all on write) and could never reproduce input bytes because offsets were discarded; 1.0 is the same public API on the offsets-first engine.

nodes.label: Migrating from dicom-parser
nodes.rationale: The dicom-parser repository is dormant; its tokenizer lives on inside dcmjs and currently parses faster than the published dicom-parser@1.8.21 on every corpus file. No compatibility shim will be published under the dicom-parser npm name; the raw tier is not yet public (a dcmjs/parser subpath is roadmap work).

nodes.label: Upstream divergence #7: undefined-length-only implicit SQ peek (readDicomElementImplicit.js, AD-1 2026-08-02)
nodes.rationale: The isSequence() data peek (first 4 value bytes = item tag / sequence delimiter) applies only to undefined-length dictionary-unknown elements, where framing genuinely needs it. Upstream also peeked defined-length elements, which (a) contradicted the dcmjs semantic contract (decodeCore.resolveVrInstance, eager parity: defined lengths are never promoted to SQ) and (b) threw on defined-length values that merely resemble item/delimiter tags (e.g. pixel data starting with FFFE bytes) or are shorter than the 4-byte peek.
